message.content:
In /bench/repo (Go project, memos fork), answer with exact path:line citations:

(1) Find where the MySQL database driver is constructed (probably a NewDB/New function in store/db/mysql/). Then search the ENTIRE codebase for every call site of that constructor (grep for the package name and constructor, e.g. `mysql.NewDB`, `mysql.New`). Determine whether it is constructed anywhere OUTSIDE the driver-selection factory (likely store/db/db.go NewDBDriver). Include test files in your search and note whether hits are tests or production. List every hit with path:line.

(2) When a user is deleted, are their emoji reactions removed by (a) explicit Go code, (b) a database-level rule (ON DELETE CASCADE in schema/migrations), or (c) not at all? Check: store/user_delete.go and store/user.go DeleteUser code paths; each SQL driver's user delete implementation (store/db/sqlite, mysql, postgres); the schema/migration files under store/migration for the reaction table definition (look for foreign keys / cascade); and any vacuum/cleanup code that deletes orphaned reactions. Report exactly what you checked with path:line for each.

Return concise findings with path:line.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Findings.

## (1) MySQL driver constructor and its call sites

**Constructor:** `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/mysql.go:20` — `func NewDB(profile *profile.Profile) (store.Driver, error)`

**Every `NewDB` reference in the repo (all three drivers, incl. test files):**

| path:line | what | prod/test |
|---|---|---|
| `/bench/repo/store/db/db.go:22` | `driver, err = mysql.NewDB(profile)` | production (factory) |
| `/bench/repo/store/db/db.go:20` | `driver, err = sqlite.NewDB(profile)` | production (factory) |
| `/bench/repo/store/db/db.go:24` | `driver, err = postgres.NewDB(profile)` | production (factory) |
| `/bench/repo/store/deployment_config_test.go:416` | `sqlite.NewDB(p)` | test |
| `/bench/repo/store/demo_seed_test.go:24` | `sqlite.NewDB(p)` | test |
| `/bench/repo/store/test/store.go:28` and `:50` | `db.NewDBDriver(profile)` | test helper |
| `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/memo_service_benchmark_test.go:70` | `db.NewDBDriver(testProfile)` | test |

**Answer:** `mysql.NewDB` is constructed in exactly ONE place — `/bench/repo/store/db/db.go:22`, inside the `NewDBDriver` factory (`/bench/repo/store/db/db.go:14`). There are **zero** call sites outside the factory, including zero in test files. (Only `sqlite.NewDB` is called directly outside the factory, and only from tests.) The other non-constructor `mysql.` hits are the `go-sql-driver/mysql` library (`mysql.ParseDSN` at `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/mysql.go:30,73`) and testcontainers (`/bench/repo/store/test/containers.go:101-105`), not the local package.

## (2) Reactions on user deletion: (a) explicit Go code

Reactions **are** removed, by explicit Go code in each driver's `DeleteUser` transaction. Not by DB cascade, and there is no vacuum/orphan-cleanup code (`grep -rn "vacuum\|Vacuum" --include=*.go` returned no files).

**Store entry point (checked):**
- `/bench/repo/store/user.go:171` — `Store.DeleteUser` delegates to `s.driver.DeleteUser` at `:172`, then cache cleanup at `:179`.
- `/bench/repo/store/user_delete.go` — contains only the `DeleteUserResult` type, failpoint helpers, and `deleteUserCache` (`:39`). **No reaction logic here.**
- `/bench/repo/store/driver.go:48` — driver interface method.

**Driver implementations (two reaction deletes each, both inside one transaction):**

| driver | orchestrator | reactions on the user's memos (by anyone) | reactions authored by the user (anywhere) |
|---|---|---|---|
| sqlite | `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:92` (calls at `:96`, `:102`) | `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:383` | `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:401` |
| postgres | `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:92` (`:96`, `:102`) | `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:383` | `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:401` |
| mysql | `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:92` (`:96`, `:102`) | `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:420` | `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:438` |

Content IDs are built as `"memos/" + memo.UID` at `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:515` (matching the `content_id` format written by the API, `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:44`), and the memo set comes from the recursive memo-tree query (`:133`), so comments' reactions are covered too. Batched at 500 (`:14`, `:381`). Transaction is committed at `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:51`, so a failure rolls reactions back with everything else.

**Schema (checked — NO cascade on `reaction`):**
- `/bench/repo/store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:92-99`, `/bench/repo/store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql:91-98`, `/bench/repo/store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql:91-98` — `reaction` has `creator_id` / `content_id` as plain columns, one `UNIQUE(creator_id, content_id, reaction_type)`, no `FOREIGN KEY`, no `ON DELETE CASCADE`.
- Original creation migrations same: `/bench/repo/store/migration/sqlite/0.20/00__reaction.sql:2`, `/bench/repo/store/migration/postgres/0.20/00__reaction.sql:2`, `/bench/repo/store/migration/mysql/0.20/00__reaction.sql:2`.
- The only cascade in the current schema is `memo_share -> memo`: `/bench/repo/store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:109`, `/bench/repo/store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql:108`, `/bench/repo/store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql:108`. Old `user` cascades exist only in historical sqlite migrations (e.g. `/bench/repo/store/migration/sqlite/0.5/00__regenerate_foreign_keys.sql:59`) and never covered `reaction`.

**Test coverage confirming the behavior:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/user_service_delete_test.go:287-298` asserts the deleted user's memo reactions and comment reactions are empty while a third party's reaction on a foreign memo survives; `:429` asserts reactions survive a rolled-back delete.
